questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I- Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.

II- All India Radio came into being in 1936.

III- In 1976, TV was delinked from AIR and got a separate identity as Doordarshan.
options_en: I, II and III are correct
Both I and II are correct
Both II and III are correct
questions.solution_en:
All statements accurately describe the history of broadcasting in India.

· Statement I: Correct. Radio broadcasting in India began in 1923 with the Radio Club of Bombay making the first broadcast.

· Statement II: Correct. The Indian State Broadcasting Service was renamed as All India Radio (AIR) in 1936.

· Statement III: Correct. In 1976, Doordarshan was separated from All India Radio and established as an independent broadcasting organization for television.
questions.solution_hi:
All statements accurately describe the history of broadcasting in India.

· Statement I: Correct. Radio broadcasting in India began in 1923 with the Radio Club of Bombay making the first broadcast.

· Statement II: Correct. The Indian State Broadcasting Service was renamed as All India Radio (AIR) in 1936.

· Statement III: Correct. In 1976, Doordarshan was separated from All India Radio and established as an independent broadcasting organization for television.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is the only rack railway in India that was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005?
questions.solution_en:
The only rack railway in India that was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005 is the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

• The Nilgiri Mountain Railway uses a rack and pinion system to climb steep inclines, which makes it unique among the other mountain railways in India.

• It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.

questions.q_en: What is the total length of Golden Quadrilateral, built by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)?
questions.solution_en:
The Golden Quadrilateral is a national highway network connecting most of the major industrial, agricultural, and cultural centres of India. Its total length is 5,846 kilometers (3,633 miles).

Further insights:

• The Golden Quadrilateral connects the four major metropolitan cities of India: Delhi (north), Kolkata (east), Mumbai (west), and Chennai (south).

• It is the largest highway project in India and the fifth-longest in the world.

• The project was initiated in 2001 and was largely completed by 2012. It falls under the purview of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

• The network consists mostly of 4-lane and 6-lane highways, significantly improving road connectivity and reducing travel time between major cities.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following factors are responsible for railways having not developed much in the north-eastern parts of India?

I. Highly dissected topography

II. Dense forests

III. Low population density

IV. Heavy rainfall and frequent flooding
questions.solution_en:
The presence of major rivers, rugged terrain, dense forests, and frequent floods in the northeastern part of the country, along with the difficulty of laying railway lines in hilly and remote areas, has led to a limited railway network in North-East India.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q_en: As of June 2023, which of the following is the longest train route in India?
questions.solution_en:
As of June 2023, and for several years, the longest train route in India in terms of distance and travel time is operated by the Vivek Express, which runs from Dibrugarh in Assam to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Jammu Tawi-Kanyakumari: The Himsagar Express runs on this route, which was previously the longest, but the Dibrugarh-Kanyakumari route is longer.

• Guwahati-Trivandrum: This is also a very long route, but not the longest.

• Amritsar-Kochuveli: Another long-distance route, but shorter than Dibrugarh-Kanyakumari.

Further insights:

• The Dibrugarh-Kanyakumari Vivek Express (Train Nos. 15905/15906 and 22503/22504 for different frequencies/days) covers a distance of approximately 4,150 to 4,200 kilometers (the exact distance can vary slightly based on operational track alignment) and takes around 75-80 hours.

• It passes through multiple states, connecting the northeastern part of India with the southernmost tip of the mainland.

• The Vivek Express series of trains were introduced to commemorate the 150th birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.

questions.q_en: In which year was the first underground section (Vishwavidyalaya-Kashmere Gate) of the Golden Route opened in New Delhi?
questions.solution_en: The first underground section of the Delhi Metro, specifically the Vishwavidyalaya to Kashmere Gate stretch on the Yellow Line (originally referred to as part of the "Golden Route"), was opened on December 20, 2004. This marked a significant milestone in the expansion of the Delhi Metro, which began operations in 2002 with the Red Line. The Yellow Line's underground section enhanced connectivity in central Delhi. Among the given options, 2004 is the correct year.
